items.q: His name was Lawrence also, you know, and he did his, you know, askance for the tap dancer's dream.

ctx.x: Well, it was like some kind of squad, do you understand? A rank I'd say. I like to say a rank because that's what the guard officiates in the world, you see. And there was some speakers, you see. See, that's to just name a few of them. There was this -- one of Baby Lawrence's proteges -- I'm quite sure, but he didn't get enough of the tap dancer's dream, you know. He was very touched by it. He's still with us, you see. That's Bunny Briggs. And another great friend, you see, but we lost him, you see. See, they all…

too long after him -- this one. He got -- he was already suffering, you see. I mean the businessman of rhythm, you see. His name was Lawrence also, you know, and he did his, you know, askance for the tap dancer's dream.

What I'd like to know as bravery, (unintelligible) because he gave us some -- he left something for us to be, to become, you see, in the future. I mean art itself, it must retain these specimens (unintelligible). That he wanted to be -- remain remedial, see. And I think that we can continue to have it lasting, and to set records, to make books.
